metadata.name: deliverable
metadata.description: Options on tokenized equities that survive corporate actions and the closing bell

accounts.name: series
docs: Derived from its own seeds like every other series account in the
program. The handler only writes a published number and the instruction
is deliberately permissionless, but "the one series account not checked
against its seeds" is the shape of finding the rest of this audit was
made of.

accounts.name: registry
docs: Claiming premium moves the underlying share — the same asset as the
collateral — out of a series-owned vault, so it takes the same gate and
the same kill switch every other value-moving path takes. It used to
take neither, which made "set it and every gated action refuses" false
of the one instruction that could empty a vault while the venue was
paused, the market shut and a hook attached.

accounts.name: primary_oracle
docs: registered with, which binds the account by address as well as by owner.

accounts.name: quote_mint
docs: What exercise is paid in. Not hardcoded: the quote asset is a listing
decision, and a venue that bakes one in cannot list against anything
else without a redeploy.

accounts.name: option_mint
docs: One option token is one contract, so it has no decimals to round.

accounts.name: collateral_vault
docs: Anchor sizes this from the mint's own required account extensions, which
is how the 175-byte xStock token account gets allocated correctly
without the program knowing that number.

accounts.name: series
docs: Derived from its own seeds, like every other series account. It is only
ever read here, and the position PDA is seeded by `series.key()` so a
forged series would produce a different position — but "the one series
account not checked against its seeds" is not a distinction worth
keeping, and `constraints_test` now enforces that there are none.

instructions.name: probe_security
docs: Ask the gate for its verdict and record it. Succeeds either way, which
is the only way a refusal can be counted — every other caller reverts.

instructions.name: probe_session
docs: Session resolution for a calendar, as a transaction anyone can send. The
answer is free to compute off-chain from the same account, but having it
on-chain means a refusal can be pointed at rather than argued about.

accounts.name: underlying_mint
docs: The security *is* its mint. One security per mint, forever.

accounts.name: security
docs: Carried for one reason: without it there is nothing to bind the calendar
to. `OptionSeries` does not store a calendar id, so the only check on
the account that decides whether the exercise window has run out was
that it is *a* calendar — and a writer who hands in one that says the
window is over takes the collateral back before any holder can exercise.

accounts.name: primary_oracle
docs: registered with, which checks the account's **address**, its owning
program, its discriminator and its length before reading a byte of it.
Unchecked here and checked there because the adapter is chosen by the
registration, not by the account list.

accounts.name: secondary_oracle
docs: with a single declared source — it is never read in that case, and the
gate refuses regardless.

accounts.name: premium_vault
docs: The premium vault's balance is half of the accumulator's input, so it
has to be present at every write: premium that arrived before these
contracts existed must be credited to the writers who carried the
obligation for it *before* the denominator moves.

types.name: CalendarEntry
docs: A single deviation from the regular weekday session.

fields.name: date_key
docs: `(year << 16) | (month << 8) | day`.
The year is load-bearing. Pyth publishes its schedule as bare MMDD, and
keying on that meant every entry fired in every subsequent year until
somebody rewrote the table: Labor Day 2026 is 7 September, so in 2027 an
ordinary Tuesday read as closed — and Labor Day 2027 is the 6th, which
was not in the table at all, so the program reported a regular session
on a day the exchange was shut. The second direction is the dangerous
one: the session gate passes and the refusal falls through to a
staleness check that a weekend-fresh timestamp satisfies.

fields.name: kind
docs: [`ENTRY_CLOSED`] or [`ENTRY_EARLY_CLOSE`].

fields.name: close_minute
docs: Minutes past local midnight, meaningful only for an early close.

fields.name: strike
docs: The strike actually charged, after the multiplier re-cut.

types.name: HaltState
docs: Attested halt state for a security.
A halt is the one condition no on-chain source can tell us: `PriceUpdateV2`
dropped the legacy `PriceStatus` enum, so halted, closed, outage and early
close are indistinguishable from staleness alone. It therefore arrives
signed by the registry's attestor and is stored, not inferred.

fields.name: since_ts
docs: When the halt began, as reported by the source. Kept after the halt is
lifted, because a settlement window has to be able to subtract the
minutes it covered — otherwise clearing a halt erases the evidence that
it was ever set.

fields.name: attested_ts
docs: When the attestor signed it. Read, not decorative: an attestation older
than [`crate::constants::HALT_ATTESTATION_MAX_AGE_SECS`] has stopped
being a claim about the present and the gate stops honouring it.

fields.name: source
docs: Which feed the attestation came from.

fields.name: lifted_ts
docs: When the halt stopped being in force, zero while it is in force. Set by
an explicit clear; a halt that is simply never refreshed ends on its own
at `attested_ts + HALT_ATTESTATION_MAX_AGE_SECS`.

types.name: MarketCalendar
docs: The exchange schedule, committed on-chain.
We commit the price publisher's own published schedule rather than our own,
so the gate cannot disagree with the feed it guards.

fields.name: id
docs: Identifies the calendar in its PDA seed; `0` is US equities.

fields.name: version
docs: Bumped whenever entries change, so an indexer can tell which schedule a
past refusal was decided under.

types.name: Observation
docs: A price as the gate sees it. `price * 10^expo` is the value in USD.

fields.name: conf
docs: Half-width of the source's uncertainty band, in the same units as
`price`. Zero from a source that publishes no band at all — see
[`OracleSource::reports_confidence`], because zero is an absence of
information and not a claim of exactness.

fields.name: option_mint
docs: Minted 1:1 with contracts, zero decimals. Burned on exercise.

fields.name: collateral_vault
docs: Holds the raw underlying that backs every written contract.

fields.name: premium_vault
docs: Premium, denominated in the underlying share. A covered call written
here accumulates the share itself.

fields.name: quote_vault
docs: Exercise proceeds, in the quote asset.

fields.name: expiry_ts
docs: Validated at creation to land inside a regular session.

fields.name: strike0
docs: Quote units per UI unit — per adjusted share — at creation.

fields.name: multiplier_at_mint
docs: The mint's effective multiplier when the series was created. Immutable:
it is half of the invariant.

fields.name: contract_raw_size
docs: Raw units of the underlying one contract covers. Immutable, and raw
rather than UI precisely so a split cannot change what is delivered.

fields.name: settlement_window_minutes
docs: Length of the exercise window, in minutes of open-market time.

fields.name: adjust_on_corporate_action
docs: False writes an unadjusted series: the strike ignores the mint. Every
options venue on tokenized equities today writes one of these by
omission. Being able to express it is what makes the invariant
falsifiable instead of merely asserted.

fields.name: quote_collected
docs: Quote units taken in by exercises, before writers claim them.

fields.name: premium_claimed_total
docs: Premium already paid out, so a later claimant sees the same denominator.

fields.name: window_opened_ts
docs: First instant after expiry at which the gate allowed an exercise. Zero
until one does; informational, the window itself is computed.

fields.name: acknowledged_multiplier
docs: The multiplier the last `acknowledge_adjustment` reported.

fields.name: contracts_assigned_total
docs: Contracts already assigned to writers who have settled.
Assignment has to sum to exactly `contracts_exercised`: pro rata over
integers rounds *every* writer down, so the writers collectively reclaim
more raw collateral than the vault holds and whoever settles after it
dries takes the loss. The running total is what makes the sum exact.

fields.name: premium_per_contract_acc
docs: Premium accrued per contract since the series was listed, scaled by
[`SCALE`], monotonic.
Premium is time-weighted rather than split by the book as it stands at
claim time: an accumulator that only ever moves forward, credited before
`contracts_written` changes, means a writer can claim exactly the
premium that arrived while their contracts were outstanding and nothing
else. Splitting by the instantaneous book let a writer who arrived after
the premium did take a share of it, in the same transaction that opened
their position.

fields.name: premium_credited_total
docs: Premium already folded into the accumulator. The difference between this
and the live pool is what the next accrual credits, so the remainder
integer division leaves behind rolls forward instead of stranding.

types.name: OracleBinding
docs: What a security is allowed to be priced from.
Scope publishes several entries per name on one account, and two of them are
sourced differently: the `PythLazer` entry carries Pyth's own number, and the
`Checked` entry is a `CappedFloored` composition whose cap and floor come
from Chainlink — so once the bound binds, the two entries are genuinely two
vendors. Verified live on 2026-09-22: AAPLx `Checked` 317 printed 340.098163,
exactly the ChainlinkX entry at 258, while `PythLazer` 315 printed 340.670950.
Binding both is therefore the normal case, not a luxury.
A single source is representable, because one will sometimes be all there is,
but it has to be spelled out — and the gate still refuses to act on it. An
options venue that settles against one unfalsifiable number is a venue that
settles against whatever that number says.

fields.name: raw_shortfall
docs: Raw units this writer was owed and the vault could not pay.
Zero for every ordinary settlement: assignment conserves, so the vault
holds exactly what the unassigned writers are owed. It can only be
non-zero if the underlying left the vault by a route this program does
not control — a permanent-delegate seizure — and in that case it must be
on the wire rather than absorbed silently by whoever settles last.

types.name: Registry
docs: Program-wide configuration. One per deployment.

fields.name: authority
docs: May create calendars and register securities. It may **not** repoint a
security's oracle sources: `security.sources` is written once at
registration and there is no instruction to change it.

fields.name: attestor
docs: The only key whose halt attestations the program accepts.

fields.name: paused
docs: Kill switch. Set it and every gated action refuses — which is every
value-moving instruction except `settle_expired`, deliberately, so that
pausing the venue cannot strand a writer's collateral.

fields.name: underlying_mint
docs: The Token-2022 mint this security *is*. Also its PDA seed.

fields.name: symbol
docs: ASCII, right-padded with zeroes: "AAPLx".

fields.name: calendar_id
docs: Which committed exchange calendar gates it.

fields.name: decimals
docs: Copied from the mint so a reader does not have to unpack it.

fields.name: observed_multiplier
docs: The multiplier in force at the last sync, fixed-point 1e12.

fields.name: pending_multiplier
docs: A scheduled change, or zero when there is none pending.

fields.name: multiplier_epoch
docs: Increments whenever `observed_multiplier` moves, so an indexer can count
corporate actions without diffing every sync.

fields.name: refusals
docs: Counted by `probe_security`, which is the only path that can record a
refusal: an instruction that refuses reverts, so its own counter goes
with it. The refused transaction's logs carry the `Refused` event.

types.name: StrikeAdjusted
docs: Emitted by `acknowledge_adjustment`. Correctness does not depend on this
ever being sent; the UI and the indexers do.

types.name: WriterPosition
docs: One writer's obligation against a series.
The receipt is this account rather than a token. A writer's position is a
short option plus the collateral standing behind it; minting a transferable
receipt would let the obligation be sold away from the collateral backing
it, and then the venue would have to chase whoever holds the paper.

fields.name: contracts
docs: Contracts written, which is also this writer's share of assignment.

fields.name: raw_collateral
docs: Raw underlying deposited, always `contracts * contract_raw_size`.

fields.name: premium_claimed
docs: Premium already taken, in underlying raw units.

fields.name: premium_debt
docs: The accumulator level this position is paid up to, scaled by [`SCALE`].
Raised on every write, by the accumulator's value at that moment times
the contracts written, so premium that arrived before those contracts
existed is not claimable against them. This is the whole of the
time-weighting: without it, writing one contract a second before expiry
bought a pro-rata share of every premium the series had ever earned.
